description: v2.1.0 section 22 lists ParticipationPolicyDef as a Definition Layer object, but section 15 only spells out the runtime ParticipationResult type (15.4) and the general mode/basis distinctions (15.1-15.3). REVISED JUDGMENT CALL (2026-08-08 review): participation structure (principal/co_principal/instigator/aider and their basis) is shared General Part doctrine, not something that should be re-declared per offense -- an earlier draft keyed this to a single 'offense' id, which risked every OffenseDef growing its own copy of the same co-principal/instigator structure instead of sharing one. This schema now declares participation modes as a standalone, offense-agnostic policy; an offense that needs to restrict or reshape the default only does so via OffenseDef.participation_constraints (offense_def.schema.json), which stays empty for the ordinary case.

mode_subsumptions.description: Authored precedence when the same participant satisfies more than one participation mode for one offense realization. A dominant attribution mode subsumes a derivative one on the participant it shares; the co-principal group itself is never subsumed. Raw assessments remain auditable; only the subsumed mode is omitted from compiled liability links.

attributable_slots.description: Which fixed slots can be satisfied via ATTRIBUTE(other co-principal's conduct) rather than this actor's own conduct -- section 15.2's example attributes property_taking(by=乙) to 甲 and violence(by=甲) to 乙, both under 'conduct'. Default here (no offense pinned) lists the slots this generally applies to; an offense that needs a narrower set overrides it in OffenseDef.participation_constraints.

establishes_predicate_refs.description: Predicate truths entailed by a validated TRUE co-principal group itself; these are symbolic outputs of the participation relation, not neural guesses.

requires_conclusion.description: Pinned, not a free choice among conclusion_type's three values. Section 15.3 is explicit that the principal's personal culpability defenses do not defeat the instigator/aider dependency, i.e. the required level is offense_realization, never offense_establishment or liability_result -- letting an author freely pick liability_result here would let a definition silently encode the exact TYPE ERROR section 15.4 exists to catch, and the type checker (step 2) would then have nothing structurally wrong to reject. If a genuine counter-example ever needs a different level, that is a v2.1.0 grammar change (open a new Open Question), not a value an author chooses per-offense.

requires.description: 8th schema addendum (2026-08-08, step 6C): the derivative participant's OWN requirement (e.g. 교사의 고의, 방조행위 존재) -- evaluated against the participant's own case truths, never the principal's. Required, not optional, unlike most addenda in this project: `requires_conclusion` only pins WHICH typed principal state the mode depends on, it says nothing about the participant's own act/intent, so an instigator/aider mode with no `requires` would let case-time Elements be satisfied by the principal's OffenseRealization alone -- an accessory liable purely because the principal succeeded, with nothing authored about the accessory's own conduct. Mirrors completion_policy_def.schema.json's states.*.requires (same grammar, same leaf-kind restriction to ground_fact/legal_element).
